# Energy Is Money. Money Is Memory. We Just Made Remembering the Most Expensive Thing on Earth.

**The AI buildout is not a compute story. It is the largest act of memory-making in human history. And the thing that decides what humanity keeps is now a queue position at a utility.**

---

## The Parallel Nobody Sees

Here is the argument in three lines. Read it twice.

> **Energy becomes money.** (Soddy, 1926. Satoshi, 2009.)
> **Money is memory.** (Kocherlakota, 1998. Graeber, 2011.)
> **Therefore: energy is memory with extra steps. We just removed the steps.**

That is the whole essay. Everything below is the proof.

![Energy = Money = Memory — The Three-Way Equivalence](/manus-storage/energy-money-memory-chart_bd2d497b.png)

*Left: The same land, different price tag. Bitcoin miners paid $0.8M/MW in 2010. AI clusters pay $8–15M/MW in 2026 for the same grid connection. Right: The three-way equivalence — energy, money, and memory are the same scarcity wearing different clothes.*

---

## What I know about money is that it keeps getting erased

I have made and lost more money than most people on this planet will ever see. Not once. Several times, in both directions, and I have never gotten used to either one.

My own website says I was wrong about the timing and right about everything else for twenty-five years. That is a joke I wrote about myself, and it is also the most expensive sentence in my life. Being early is indistinguishable from being wrong right up until it isn't, and the market settles up in cash long before it settles up in credit.

I put the first URL on live television. I built webcasts before anyone was watching. I was making online video half a decade before YouTube existed. Every one of those was correct. Several of them were catastrophic.

So I have had reason to think carefully about what money actually is, because mine kept disappearing.

Here is what I concluded. I wrote it down in 2010 without understanding what I had written. I opened an essay with the old parable about Heaven and Hell — same room, same table groaning with food, same four-foot utensils too long for anyone to feed themselves. In Hell everyone starves holding a full spoon. In Heaven they reach across and feed each other.

I thought I was writing about business relationships. I was actually writing about accounting. The only thing that distinguishes the two rooms is whether the people in them **remember each other.**

I have watched my net worth go to a number I will not repeat and then go to something considerably worse than zero, and the thing that never moved through any of it was the ledger nobody keeps in dollars. Who picked up the phone. Whose call I returned in 2004 and who returned mine in 2011 when I badly needed it. What people remembered I had done for them when I could no longer do anything for them at all.

**The money was erasable. The memory was not.**

That is not a greeting card. It is a balance sheet observation. And it is the same argument I have been making since the long spoons. I just finally found the physics underneath it.

---

## 1926: Soddy says wealth is energy

Frederick Soddy won a Nobel Prize in chemistry and then, to the considerable annoyance of economists, wrote a book about money.

In *Wealth, Virtual Wealth and Debt* (1926), he made an argument that was ignored for fifty years and has aged like a threat. Real wealth, he said, is what you get when you apply energy to matter and transform it into something useful — buildings, food, machines. Everything else is virtual wealth: money, credit, debt, claims on other people's future output.

He was treated as a crank for decades. But Soddy did not say energy is *like* money. He said money is a **shadow cast by energy**, and confusing the two is how civilizations get into trouble.

Hold that.

---

## 2009: Satoshi makes it literal

For eighty-three years Soddy's claim stayed metaphorical. Then somebody built the metaphor.

Proof of work does exactly one strange and beautiful thing: it converts joules into an unforgeable claim. Not symbolically. Mechanically. You spend electricity, you produce a number, and that number is expensive precisely because the electricity was expensive. Soddy's argument, compiled and shipped.

Bitcoin is the first money in history whose cost of production is stated in kilowatt-hours on purpose, in public, continuously.

And here is the part the industry took fifteen years to notice. The miners were never really in the mining business. They were in the business of acquiring energized land with grid rights during a period when nobody else wanted it.

The machines were worth $700,000 to $1 million per megawatt. What replaced them costs $8 million to $15 million per megawatt. **The building was never the asset. The connection was.**

![The bottleneck: where money becomes memory](/manus-storage/energy-memory-bottleneck_1286ea43.jpg)

*The narrow neck is not the chip. It is not the building. It is the transformer in the parking lot — a steel box on a concrete pad — and behind it, a filing cabinet at a regional grid operator. Electrical equipment is under ten percent of data center cost and one hundred percent of the bottleneck.*

---

## 1998: An economist proves money is memory

There is a paper by Narayana Kocherlakota with one of the great titles in economics: *Money Is Memory.* The argument is austere and, once you see it, unforgettable.

Anything money can do, a perfect communal record of who did what for whom could also do. Money is not a thing. Money is a technology for **remembering obligations** in a society too large to remember them personally.

David Graeber came at it from anthropology and landed in the same place. Credit came first. Coins came later. Before there was currency there were ledgers, tallies, debts held in the head of a village. Money is what we invented because we could not remember each other at scale.

So run the chain:

| Step | Who Proved It | What It Means |
|------|--------------|---------------|
| **Energy → Money** | Soddy (1926), Satoshi (2009) | Real wealth is stored energy. Bitcoin made it mechanical. |
| **Money → Memory** | Kocherlakota (1998), Graeber (2011) | Money is a ledger of obligations — a memory technology. |
| **Therefore: Energy → Memory** | The AI buildout (2026) | We removed the steps. GPU clusters convert watts directly into recall. |

---

## 2026: The steps come out

Here is what an AI training run actually is, stripped of the mythology.

You take electricity. You use it to compress an enormous quantity of human output into a set of weights. Then you spend more electricity retrieving from those weights on demand. That is not a metaphor for memory. That is memory — encoding, storage, retrieval, the same three verbs a neuroscientist would use.

The IEA's April 2026 update puts global data center electricity consumption at roughly 485 terawatt-hours in 2025, doubling to 950 terawatt-hours by 2030. Something close to three percent of all electricity generated on this planet, dedicated to the industrial production of recall.

**We have built the first economy in which remembering is a line item on the grid.**

And because it is on the grid, it is rationed. American interconnection queues hold 2,060 gigawatts waiting to connect, with a median wait approaching five years. Of everything that asked to connect between 2000 and 2019, roughly nineteen percent had actually connected by the end of 2024.

Read that number again with the thesis in hand. **Four out of five requests to build memory capacity did not happen.**

## The bottleneck just got a name

On June 18, 2026, a helium-cooled nuclear reactor called Ward 250 went critical in the Utah desert. It was the first reactor to do that outside a national laboratory. Its electricity then ran an Nvidia Blackwell system in a live demo.

Weeks later, Sequoia wired $1 billion into the company that built it. Valar Atomics is now valued at $6 billion, triple its April mark. A $200 million credit facility takes the total to $1.2 billion.

The thesis is not "build a better reactor."

It is "stop building reactors like construction projects and start manufacturing them like products."

One reactor is a project. A fleet is a production line.

Valar still needs an NRC licence before it sells a single watt. The hard part is ahead. But the market just told you something: when a nuclear startup powers a Blackwell chip in a live demo, Sequoia does not wait for the paperwork.

AI data centres are pulling more power than grids can hand over. The 2,060 gigawatts sitting in American interconnection queues is not a planning problem. It is a physics problem. You cannot negotiate with the speed of light or the capacity of a transmission line.

Energy is the real bottleneck in AI. Not compute. Not talent. Not capital. Power.

And the people who solve the power problem will decide what gets remembered.

---

## Memory has always been expensive. That is the whole problem.

Before the printing press, remembering anything required a human being to spend a life copying. Monasteries were memory infrastructure. The energy source was calories and devotion, and the throughput was one manuscript at a time. What survived antiquity was not what was most true or most beautiful. It was what somebody was willing to feed a scribe to keep.

Every culture that has ever lost something lost it because the energy budget for remembering ran out. Languages die when nobody can afford to teach them. Techniques disappear one funeral at a time.

> What we remember has never been decided by what is worth remembering. It has been decided by who was willing to pay the energy bill.

Now the bill is a power purchase agreement and the scribe is a GPU. The mechanism did not change. Only the scale, and the honesty of the accounting.

---

## The provocation

If energy is money, and money is memory, then the allocation of electricity is the allocation of remembrance.

Which means every gigawatt contract signed this year is a vote on what humanity keeps.

Nobody is casting that vote consciously. There is no committee. There is a queue at a regional transmission organization, a backlog at a turbine manufacturer, and a spreadsheet at a hyperscaler. The most consequential curatorial decision in human history is being made by procurement.

And the thing being remembered is overwhelmingly whatever was already legible to the training pipeline — which is to say, whatever was already written down, already digitized, already English.

The long spoons are back. The table is full. The question is whether we remember to reach across it.

---

## What do you think?

I have been sitting with this argument for a while and I am not sure I have the conclusion right. Here is what I am genuinely uncertain about:

**Is the allocation of memory capacity the most important political question of the next decade — or am I overstating it?**

If you work in energy, infrastructure, AI, or you have just watched something disappear because nobody could afford to remember it — I want to hear from you. Reply to this, or find me at [tony@impactsoul.is](mailto:tony@impactsoul.is). I read everything.

---

### Keep Reading

- [Business at the Speed of Light — What Is a Millisecond Worth?](https://tonygreenberg.com/blog/business-at-the-speed-of-light-millisecond-worth) — RampRate's 2011 piece on the I/O bottleneck. The bottleneck moved. The argument didn't.
- [The $1,000/Hour Hold — A Manifesto Against the Companies That Steal Your Time](https://tonygreenberg.com/blog/the-1000-hour-hold) — What happens when systems are optimized for the wrong variable.
- [Only Time Buys Trust](https://tonygreenberg.com/blog/only-time-buys-trust) — The original essay. Memory that survived contact with time.
- [Enterprise Blockchain: Can Big Business Co-opt an Existential Threat?](https://tonygreenberg.com/blog/enterprise-blockchain-can-big-business-co-opt) — The last time a new infrastructure layer rewrote who controls the ledger.
- [Why Good Service Is All About Trust](https://tonygreenberg.com/blog/why-good-service-is-all-about-trust) — The accounting that doesn't show up in dollars.
- [Human OS 2.0](https://tonygreenberg.com/humanos) — What happens when intelligence becomes abundant and attention becomes scarce.

---

*The same structural capture — incumbents who profit from your ignorance of what is possible — shows up in healthcare too. I wrote about it in [Your Blood Lies Without Your DNA](/blog/your-blood-lies-without-your-dna). Different domain. Same dynamic.*

# Your Blood Lies Without Your DNA

**Twenty-five years benchmarking broken systems. The most broken one in 2026 is responsible for reading your blood.**

---

For twenty-five years I have sat in the middle of the trust layer between buyers and sellers. Not as an advisor. As the intermediary. $10B+ in transactions across Microsoft, Disney, Goldman Sachs, Nike. My job has always been the same: find where the relationship is broken and build something better. I am a business person and an impact futurist. I see around corners for a living.

In 2026, the worst-performing vendor I encountered was not a cloud provider. It was not a telco. It was Quest Diagnostics — $11 billion in annual revenue, 22% market share in U.S. clinical diagnostics — and I was standing in their waiting room on a Tuesday morning, re-entering information into a kiosk that already had all of it.

Two weeks to book the appointment. The system already knew my name, physician, lab order, and insurance. It asked me to type it all in again anyway. A staff member said a manager would come. The manager did not come.

Then Giselle appeared. She found my second lab order that the system had lost. She fixed everything. She treated me with the kind of simple, complete dignity that you do not forget because it is so rarely delivered in institutions that are supposed to be built around human care.

**Quest does not have a people problem. It has a systems problem. Giselle proved that.**

Quest charges $11 billion a year and holds a 1.7-star Trustpilot rating. That gap is the entire story of what happens when a vendor's incentives are structurally misaligned with the customer's outcome. The billing department is optimized for collections. The kiosk is optimized for reducing labor cost. None of them are optimized for the human being who showed up needing a blood draw.

---

## The Stack I Actually Use

Here is my procurement verdict on the preventative health industry, written the way I write vendor assessments: here is who is winning, who is pretending to win, and exactly what to buy at what price.

**Function Health** is the platform I use as my foundation. 160+ biomarkers, a phlebotomist at your door, a physician who reads your results, and a dashboard that actually explains what the numbers mean. $365 per year. Use code **AGREENBERG10** at [my.functionhealth.com/signup?code=AGREENBERG10](https://my.functionhealth.com/signup?code=AGREENBERG10&_saasquatch=AGREENBERG10&d=FHREF25) and you get 10% off. I get a referral credit. Full transparency.

**DEXA scan** — BodySpec or DexaFit, $50 to $75. Full body composition: lean mass, fat mass, bone density, visceral fat. More useful than any BMI calculation ever invented, and cheaper than dinner. Book one this week.

**DUTCH Complete** — dutchtest.com. The hormone test that actually works. Dried urine, 35+ markers, cortisol curve, sex hormones, melatonin. If you have ever been told your hormones are "normal" and felt anything but, this is the test that finds the real picture.

**OmegaQuant Complete** — omegaquant.com. 24 fatty acid markers from a red blood cell membrane sample. The omega-3 index is the single most underrated cardiovascular biomarker in mainstream medicine. Most people are deficient. Most doctors never test it.

**Neko Health** — nekohealth.com. Full-body scan, 50+ health markers, 45-minute appointment. Raised $700 million in 2024. Not yet widely available but worth the waitlist.

---

## The Part Nobody Tells You: Blood Without DNA Is Half the Picture

Here is the thing the preventative health industry mostly skips.

Your biomarkers tell you what is happening. Your DNA tells you why — and more importantly, what to do about it. Absorption rates, metabolism pathways, drug sensitivities, nutrient deficiencies that no amount of supplementation will fix because your body is genetically wired to process them differently.

Two people with identical blood panels can need completely different interventions. The difference is in the genome. Your blood lies without your DNA — not because the numbers are wrong, but because the numbers are incomplete without the context that only your genetic code provides.

I am working on access to anonymous DNA coupon codes for people who want to run this analysis without their genetic data sitting in a commercial database. If you want one, email [tony@impactsoul.is](mailto:tony@impactsoul.is) with the subject line "Anonymous DNA Coupon Code." I will send what I have.

---

## The Procurement Verdict

| Vendor | What It Does | Cost | My Rating |
|--------|-------------|------|-----------|
| Function Health | 160+ biomarkers, physician review | $365/yr | Buy. Use AGREENBERG10. |
| DEXA Scan | Body composition, bone density | $50-75 | Buy immediately. |
| DUTCH Complete | Hormone panel, cortisol curve | $350-400 | Buy if hormones feel off. |
| OmegaQuant | Fatty acid / omega-3 index | $100-150 | Buy. Underrated. |
| Neko Health | Full-body scan, 50+ markers | ~$300 | Waitlist now. |
| Quest Diagnostics | Volume blood processing | Insurance | Use only when required. |

The system that was supposed to read your biology has been optimized for everything except you. The vendors above built the alternative. The only thing standing between you and a complete picture of your own health is the decision to start.

Start with the blood. Then add the DNA. Then you have a map.

---

**Tony Greenberg** is Founder and CEO of [RampRate](https://ramprate.com) and Founder of [ImpactSoul](https://impactsoul.is). Twenty-five years benchmarking broken systems. Only Time Buys Trust.


---

## The Scoreboard Nobody Hangs in the Lobby

For twenty-five years I have been the trust layer between buyers and sellers at scale. $10B+ in transactions. Microsoft. Disney. Goldman Sachs. Nike. I am not a procurement advisor. I am the person who sees what the relationship is actually doing to you and builds the bridge to something better. That is a very specific lens. And through that lens, Quest Diagnostics is one of the most structurally broken vendor relationships I have ever seen.

I want to show you something.

# I Made Money Today on Psychedelics. I'm Not Celebrating.

### A letter to Rick Doblin and the field — on the death of Tina Sodhi, the arrest of Dr. Samuel Lee, and the paradox of the most important day in psychedelic medicine history.

---
> 🔴 **LIVE — This article is being updated in real time as new information comes in.** Last updated: July 16, 2026. Refresh for the latest.

---


> **Disclosure:** On July 16, 2026 — the day this article was published — Eli Lilly announced the acquisition of AtaiBeckley for $2.8 billion upfront. The author is an early investor in Beckley Psytech (acquired by atai Life Sciences in November 2025 to form AtaiBeckley) and holds shares that increased in value as a direct result of this transaction. The author also holds investments in the following psychedelic medicine companies mentioned in this article: MycoMedica Life Sciences, Wake Network, Radicle Science, and Tripp. These financial interests are declared in the interest of full transparency and do not alter the analysis, conclusions, or calls to action in this letter.

> **EDITOR'S SUMMARY:** On July 14, 2026 — the same day Eli Lilly announced a $2.8 billion upfront acquisition of psychedelic biotech AtaiBeckley — Dr. Samuel Lee was charged with felony manslaughter for the February 2025 death of Tina Sodhi during a self-branded "Heart Protocol" ceremony in Miami Beach. The author is an early investor in Beckley Psytech, the company that merged with atai Life Sciences to form AtaiBeckley, and a 20-year acquaintance of Rick Doblin. This open letter calls for five minimum safety standards and a citizen medicine movement.

Tina Sodhi was 51 years old. She paid $2,000 to attend a three-day retreat at Sabia Wellness House in Miami Beach. She signed a waiver. She trusted someone with her life. She was found unresponsive in a rooftop sauna in February 2025. She was pronounced dead at the scene.

The Miami-Dade Medical Examiner determined she died from extreme dehydration caused by a simultaneous combination of MDMA, ketamine, and DMT — plus a parasite cleanser administered before the ceremony — in prolonged heat exposure. Dr. Samuel Lee, the licensed psychiatrist who administered those compounds, has been charged with second-degree felony manslaughter. Court records also show Lee told an officer he was not performing the ceremony under his medical license — and his Florida medical license was expired at the time of Tina Sodhi's death.

I am deeply sad writing this. That is where I need to start.

Ask yourself: if you had been in that room, what would you have done differently? And more importantly — what would have stopped you from walking in?

---

## Rick — This Moment Belongs to You

You founded [MAPS](https://maps.org) in 1986 because the DEA placed MDMA in Schedule I, overriding its own administrative law judge's recommendation that it remain available for therapeutic use. You spent four decades building the scientific, legal, and cultural foundations for the responsible use of these medicines.

This month, you said something that stopped me:

> *"We are closer than ever to psychedelics becoming legal medicines again, but what's emerging looks different from what I spent 40 years fighting for. My biggest concern now is no longer whether these therapies will be approved, but what they will look like when they arrive, and who will be able to access them. Companies are increasingly minimizing or eliminating the therapeutic component entirely, treating the drug as the product and everything around it as a cost to be cut."*
>
> — **Rick Doblin, Ph.D.**, MAPS 40th Anniversary Statement, April 2026

That warning — "treating the drug as the product and everything around it as a cost to be cut" — is the precise mechanism that killed Tina Sodhi. Dr. Lee did not eliminate the therapeutic component. He replaced it with a brand. He called it the "Heart Protocol." He charged $2,000 for access. He invented, packaged, and sold an untested compound stack as a breakthrough experience. Lee's Eternal Life Tribe had over 4,000 paying members at $55/month — a recurring revenue model built entirely on ceremonial authority.

That inversion — product over practice, novelty over wisdom, brand over reverence — is what this letter is about.

---


## Today Is July 14, 2026

This morning, [Eli Lilly announced a $2.8 billion acquisition of AtaiBeckley](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/16/eli-lilly-to-buy-psychedelics-maker-ataibeckley-2point8-billion.html) — the psychedelic biotech formed when atai Life Sciences acquired Beckley Psytech in November 2025 — a company I was a proud early investor in. It is the largest single psychedelic medicine transaction in history. Big pharma has arrived.

On this same day, Dr. Samuel Lee faces a manslaughter charge for Tina Sodhi's death.

Dr. Lee is not a fringe figure. He earned his MD at Loma Linda University School of Medicine. He completed his psychiatry residency at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center and the University of Washington. He was board-certified by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology since 2013. He worked as a psychiatrist at Kaiser Permanente. He was medical director at a licensed treatment center in Sedona, Arizona. He has a podcast. He has a following. He has a curriculum vitae that most practitioners in this field would envy.

None of that is a defense. It is an indictment.

[Read the full case file — Dr. Lee's license history, legal exposure, and the Heart Protocol business model →](/blog/the-case-file-dr-samuel-lee)

## The Body Does Not Care About Your Brand

I have invested in [MAPS](https://maps.org), [MycoMedica Life Sciences](https://mycomedica.com) (co-founded with Paul Stamets), [AtaiBeckley](https://ataibeckley.com), [Wake Network](https://wakenetwork.com), [Radicle Science](https://radicle.science), [TRIPP](https://tripp.com), and others. I have sat with these medicines myself. I am not an expert. I am a student. That distinction matters enormously here.

I recently began building the [Psychedelic Readiness Index](https://tonygreenberg.com/psychedelic-readiness-index) — a clinical screening tool covering 26 medicines across 6 safety domains — because pharmacological sequencing, interaction risk, and the balance between synthetic and natural substances is dangerously under-addressed in the retreat and ceremony space.

## Matthew Perry Died the Same Way

[Matthew Perry died in October 2023](https://www.cnbc.com/2023/12/15/matthew-perry-cause-of-death-revealed.html). Found face down in his hot tub. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner determined the cause of death was the acute effects of ketamine. His blood concentration — 3,271 nanograms per milliliter — was within the range used for surgical general anesthesia. He was alone. He was in hot water. He was dissociated from his own body. He drowned.

# Tina Sodhi Died in a Sauna.
# She Didn't Have To.

On February 10, 2025, Tina Sodhi paid $2,000 to attend a three-day "Heart Protocol" ceremony at a wellness home in Miami Beach. She was administered MDMA and ketamine. She was found unresponsive in a rooftop sauna.

The Miami-Dade Medical Examiner ruled her death: dehydration from the combination of MDMA, ketamine, prolonged heat exposure, and a pre-ceremony cleansing regimen. She had signed a waiver. It didn't save her. It didn't save the doctor either — Dr. Samuel Lee was charged with felony manslaughter on July 14, 2026.

She was not the first. She will not be the last — unless this industry decides to govern itself before the government does it for us.

What follows are not guidelines. They are the minimum standard of care this field must adopt publicly, immediately, and without exception.

---

## The Six Laws of Conscious Medicine

*These are not guidelines. They are the minimum standard of care this field must adopt publicly, immediately, and without exception.*

---

**LAW I — Water and heat kill when combined with dissociative compounds. No exceptions.** Tina Sodhi died because MDMA and ketamine were administered before sauna exposure. MDMA elevates core body temperature and suppresses heat regulation. A sauna is not spiritual in this context. It is fatal. No ceremony overrides this. No waiver makes it legal. No brand name makes it safe.

**LAW II — Compound stacking without peer-reviewed safety data is experimentation. Name it that.** MDMA, ketamine, and DMT did not kill Tina Sodhi separately. They killed her together — in a combination that had never been studied, presented as a "Heart Protocol." If there is no published safety data on the specific combination at the specific doses you are administering, you are running an experiment. Your participants did not sign up for an experiment.

**LAW III — A waiver is not informed consent.** Tina Sodhi signed a waiver. She did not understand that MDMA plus ketamine plus a sauna could kill her — because no one told her. Real informed consent requires a sober explanation of every compound and its interaction risks, written contraindications, and the right to withdraw at any stage without social pressure or financial penalty. A signature is not the same thing. Her family knows what the difference is.

**LAW IV — Credentials do not replace lineage, training, and humility.** The most dangerous practitioner in this space right now is the one who completed a weekend certification last year and charges $3,000 a seat. Ask your facilitator: Who trained you? How long? Are you still in supervision? If they cannot answer all three without defensiveness, you have your answer.

**LAW V — These medicines are singular teachers. You do not stack teachers and expect coherence.** Every tradition that has worked with these plants for centuries holds one inviolable principle: one medicine, one container, one teacher at a time. The moment you combine two medicines in one ceremony, you have stepped outside every map that exists. You are no longer facilitating. You are improvising with someone else's nervous system.

**LAW VI — A practice improves. A product just sells.** The day you stop asking "what did I miss?" is the day you become dangerous. Tina Sodhi's death was not an accident. It was the result of a practitioner who had answers instead of questions. If you are more focused on your next cohort than your last client's integration — you are running a business, not a practice. One of them has a body count.

---

**If you run retreats:** Post these six laws publicly. On your website. Before the booking page. If you will not stand behind them publicly, examine why.

**If you refer clients:** You are accountable for where you send them. Ask every operator you refer to whether they will sign these laws. Publish who will and who will not.

**If you are a client:** You have the right to ask every one of these questions before you enter any container. A facilitator who cannot answer them clearly and without defensiveness is not ready to hold you. Walk away. Tina Sodhi paid $2,000. She paid with her life.

---

> The industry will not self-regulate through good intentions. It will self-regulate through standards that the best practitioners hold publicly — and the worst are publicly measured against. Tina Sodhi deserved these laws before February 10, 2025. The next person deserves them today.

*— TonyG*

---

*Share this. Ask every facilitator you work with to sign it publicly. If they won't — that is your answer. And now you know.*

---

## A Response Worth Keeping

Within hours of publication, **Dr. Stephen Scappa** — psychiatrist & physician, powering great human potential — sent this. I am not summarizing it. I am not contextualizing it. I am printing it whole, because it is the rare thing: a real human, with real standing, saying exactly what needs to be said.

> *"Off-label prescribing depends upon and trusts the physician's judgement. Professional judgement is all too commonly diminished by good intentions — when the prescriber does not say 'no' to a patient in sometimes desperate need. Or whose pockets are full of cash and clout, as is suggested in the tragedy of Tina Sodhi and Dr. Samuel Lee.*
>
> *'Let the buyer beware' places responsibility on the patient. Better is: trust, but verify. Do not trust blindly because of a degree upon the wall.*
>
> *Hallucinogenics are now soaked in hype and money and a desire for magic. Any practitioner with their own special treatment should be examined — by the patient and the professional associations — before being let loose upon the public."*
>
> — **Dr. Stephen Scappa**, psychiatrist & physician · powering great human potential · July 16, 2026

"Do not trust blindly because of a degree upon the wall."

That is the Six Laws in one sentence.


## What These Medicines Actually Teach

The ancient Peruvian concept of ayni — sacred reciprocity — teaches that if we take without giving, we hurt ourselves and can become sick. Lee took $2,000 from a woman who trusted him with her life. He took the spiritual legitimacy of traditions that took centuries to develop. He gave nothing back except a pharmacological environment that guaranteed harm.

He approached as the teacher. He made himself the medicine. He branded his invention and charged for access. That inversion is what killed Tina Sodhi.

---


## The Paradox of This Watershed Day

[Eli Lilly's $2.8 billion acquisition of AtaiBeckley](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-16/lilly-to-buy-psychedelic-firm-ataibeckley-for-up-to-3-8-billion) validates what this field can become at its best. BPL-003 — a nasally administered 5-MeO-DMT treatment for treatment-resistant depression — is administered in a clinic, under monitoring, for about two hours. Single compound. Safe environment. Supervised. That is what responsible looks like.

And on this same day, Tina Sodhi has been dead for more than a year.

Rick, you also said this month: *"After four decades, I remain genuinely optimistic that psychedelic-assisted therapies will once again become legal. But legality was never the point. Healing was."*

That sentence is the entire argument of this letter. Legality was never the point. Healing was. And healing requires the humility to keep practicing.

---


## A Deep Bow: Ron Beller

**Ron Beller** is Rick Doblin's personal coach. He has been one of the quiet architects of this movement's credibility — not from a stage, not from a press release, but from the inside, over years, doing the unglamorous work of holding space for the people who hold space for everyone else. That work matters. This letter would not exist without people like him.

## A Note on My Standing to Write This

**Disclosure and accountability:** For over 20 years, Tony Greenberg has been a personal acquaintance of Rick Doblin and has had direct visibility inside MAPS — as an observer, supporter, and investor in MAPS Public Benefit Corporation (MAPS PBC). He is also an investor in MAPS Public Benefit Corporation (MAPS PBC), MycoMedica Life Sciences, AtaiBeckley, Wake Network, Radicle Science, and TRIPP.

This piece was written with AI assistance to raise the baton faster. This piece was written with AI assistance to raise the baton faster. Speed over polish. Accountability over silence.



*This is not an isolated failure. The same extraction pattern — a system designed to serve you, rebuilt to extract from you — shows up in how we test blood ([Your Blood Lies Without Your DNA](/blog/your-blood-lies-without-your-dna)) and in how we build AI infrastructure ([Energy Is Money. Money Is Memory.](/blog/energy-is-money-money-is-memory)). The mechanism is always the same. Only the domain changes.*

---

*[Read the pharmacological addendum — compound interactions, misnomers, and what legitimate research looks like →](/blog/heart-protocol-addendum)*

*[Read the full case file — Dr. Lee's license history, legal exposure, and the Heart Protocol business model →](/blog/the-case-file-dr-samuel-lee)*

### What Is Off-Label Prescribing?

Before Dr. Scappa's letter, a brief note for those unfamiliar with the term he uses — because understanding it is essential to understanding what he is saying.

**Off-label prescribing** is when a physician prescribes an FDA-approved medication to treat a condition, or in a way, that the FDA has not officially approved. It is legal. It is common. And it is entirely dependent on the professional judgment of the prescribing physician.

The FDA approves drugs for specific indications based on clinical trial data. But once a drug is approved, physicians may prescribe it for other conditions where evidence — sometimes strong, sometimes emerging, sometimes anecdotal — suggests benefit. Ketamine, for example, is FDA-approved as an anesthetic. Its off-label use for treatment-resistant depression is now widespread. Psilocybin is not FDA-approved for anything yet. But in clinical trial settings and, increasingly, in private practice, it is being administered off-label.

The critical point: off-label prescribing is not inherently dangerous. It is inherently dependent on the quality, integrity, and accountability of the physician making the call. When that judgment is sound, off-label prescribing saves lives. When it is compromised — by desperation, by money, by ego, by ideology — it becomes the mechanism through which harm is delivered with a medical credential attached.

### A Note on Alexander Shulgin

Before dissecting what went wrong, it\'s worth acknowledging who got it right.

[Alexander Shulgin](https://erowid.org/culture/characters/shulgin_alexander/shulgin_alexander.shtml) (1925–2014) was the chemist who re-synthesized MDMA in 1976, recognized its therapeutic potential, and introduced it to psychotherapists including Leo Zeff. His two landmark volumes, *PiHKAL (Phenethylamines I Have Known and Loved)* and *TiHKAL (Tryptamines I Have Known and Loved)*, co-authored with his wife Ann, documented the synthesis, dosing, and subjective effects of hundreds of psychoactive compounds with a rigor, honesty, and ethical seriousness that shames most of what followed.

Shulgin didn\'t brand his work. He documented it. He warned about contraindications. He argued for careful, intentional use under qualified supervision. He understood that MDMA was a tool of extraordinary delicacy, not a ceremony ingredient to be stacked with ketamine and DMT and administered in a rooftop sauna.

The field owes him its foundational vocabulary. The least it can do is honor the precision with which he used it.

### What "Protocol" Actually Means

In legitimate clinical practice, a protocol is a documented, peer-reviewed, IRB-approved procedural standard. It specifies:

- Fixed dosages with defined titration ranges
- Compound selection rationale tied to specific clinical indication
- Contraindication screening requirements (cardiac, hepatic, psychiatric, pharmacological)
- Monitoring requirements during administration
- Rescue procedures and stop criteria
- Integration support structure post-session

A published example: the Roots to Thrive ketamine-assisted therapy model delivers three structured ketamine sessions embedded in a 12-week Community of Practice, co-facilitated by a multidisciplinary team including healthcare providers, therapists, and somatic energy practitioners. That is a protocol.

> **What Lee called the "Heart Protocol" had none of this.** The word "protocol" was branding: borrowed legitimacy. White coat language placed on a ceremony with no clinical infrastructure behind it.

MDMA, ketamine, and DMT operate through entirely different receptor systems, with different risk profiles, different durations, and radically different thermoregulatory consequences. Treating them as interchangeable or additively therapeutic is pharmacologically illiterate. ### The Mechanism Nobody Is Naming: Serotonin Syndrome

The combination of MDMA and DMT represents a textbook serotonin syndrome pathway that is neither obscure nor contested:

- MDMA floods serotonin release massively. It\'s the primary mechanism of action.
- DMT agonizes serotonin 5-HT2A receptors directly
- Combined, they hit serotonin release, reuptake inhibition, and receptor agonism simultaneously
- Ketamine, added to this stack, compounds CNS depression and further impairs homeostatic regulation

Serotonin syndrome is characterized by cognitive dysfunction, autonomic instability, neuromuscular dysfunction, and hyperthermia. MDMA activates mechanisms that both conserve and generate heat while simultaneously causing peripheral vasoconstriction, closing the skin\'s heat-release valve. In a rooftop sauna, this was inevitable.

> **This is foundational pharmacology that any board-certified psychiatrist is required to know.** Shulgin documented the thermal risks of MDMA in *PiHKAL*. The peer-reviewed literature has confirmed it since the 1990s. There is no universe in which ignorance is a defense.

### Glossary

**5-HT2A Receptor**: A serotonin receptor subtype that is the primary target of classic psychedelics (psilocybin, LSD, DMT). Agonism here produces perceptual alteration, neuroplasticity, and the characteristic psychedelic experience. MDMA does not primarily act here.

**Classic Psychedelic**: A compound that produces altered consciousness primarily through 5-HT2A serotonin receptor agonism. Includes psilocybin, LSD, DMT, mescaline. Does NOT include MDMA or ketamine.

**Dissociative Anesthetic**: A compound that produces dissociation, analgesia, and amnesia through NMDA glutamate receptor antagonism. Ketamine is the primary clinical example.

**Entactogen**: A term coined by Alexander Shulgin to describe compounds that create emotional openness, empathy, and interpersonal connection through monoamine flooding. MDMA is the primary example. It isn\'t a classic psychedelic.

**Exertional Hyperpyrexia**: Life-threatening overheating caused by the combination of a warm environment and a drug that impairs thermoregulation. The mechanism that killed Tina Sodhi.

**Integration (clinical definition)**: Structured post-session therapeutic support, typically 3–12 supervised sessions with a qualified therapist, designed to metabolize and contextualize an altered-state experience.

**IRB**: Institutional Review Board. An independent ethics committee that reviews and approves research protocols involving human subjects. No IRB ever reviewed the "Heart Protocol."

**MAPS**: Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies. Founded 1986 by Rick Doblin, Ph.D. The organization responsible for the most rigorous clinical trials of psychedelic medicines conducted to date. [maps.org](https://maps.org)

**NMDA Receptor**: N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor. A glutamate receptor subtype blocked by ketamine. Entirely distinct from the serotonin receptors targeted by classic psychedelics.

**PiHKAL / TiHKAL**: *Phenethylamines I Have Known and Loved* / *Tryptamines I Have Known and Loved*. Alexander Shulgin\'s two-volume pharmacological and autobiographical record. The foundational texts of modern psychedelic chemistry. Still in print. Required reading for anyone who calls themselves a practitioner.

**Protocol (clinical definition)**: A documented, peer-reviewed procedural standard specifying dosing, contraindication screening, monitoring, rescue procedures, and integration structure. Not a brand name.

**Serotonin Syndrome**: A potentially fatal drug reaction caused by excess serotonergic activity, characterized by hyperthermia, autonomic instability, and neuromuscular dysfunction. Risk is substantially elevated by MDMA + DMT co-administration.

**Set and Setting**: The psychological mindset (set) and physical environment (setting) of a psychedelic experience. A real determinant of outcome — but not a pharmacological safety mechanism.

**Shulgin, Alexander (1925–2014)**: Chemist, pharmacologist, author. Re-synthesized MDMA in 1976 and recognized its therapeutic potential. Coined the term entactogen. Authored *PiHKAL* and *TiHKAL*. The intellectual godfather of the field, and a man who never confused branding with science.

**Stacking / Polypharmacy**: The simultaneous administration of multiple psychoactive compounds. No peer-reviewed evidence supports the specific stack used in the Lee case (MDMA + ketamine + DMT).

---

## Further Reading

Three essays that extend this argument:

**[Iboga vs. Ibogaine: The Full Paradox](/blog/iboga-ibogaine-the-full-paradox)**: The most misunderstood distinction in psychedelic medicine. One is a sacred plant with 40,000 years of ceremonial context. The other is a pharmaceutical extract. Conflating them is costing lives.

**[Psychedelics Could Become Extractive Capitalism](/blog/psychedelics-could-become-extractive-capitalism)**: Written for DoubleBlind in 2021. The warning was already there. The field didn\'t listen fast enough.

**[Human Operating System](/blog/human-operating-system)**: The framework behind this essay\'s approach: conscious satisficing over optimization, speed of relevance over perfection of argument. Why "faster is better than perfect" is not laziness — it\'s the correct response to a system that is actively harming people right now.

**[The Living Declaration](/living-declaration)**: Tony\'s personal manifesto. The values that make this letter possible: accountability over comfort, speed over silence, regenerative systems over extractive ones. If this essay landed, the Declaration is where the operating system behind it lives.

---

*Tony Greenberg, Founder, [ImpactSoul](https://impactsoul.is) · CEO, [RampRate](https://ramprate.com) · Author, [boy in the human](https://tonygreenberg.com) · Speaker alongside Ray Kurzweil, 2010*

# I Made Money Today on Psychedelics. I'm Not Celebrating.

### A letter to Rick Doblin and the field — on the death of Tina Sodhi, the arrest of Dr. Samuel Lee, and the paradox of the most important day in psychedelic medicine history.

---
> 🔴 **LIVE — This article is being updated in real time as new information comes in.** Last updated: July 16, 2026. Refresh for the latest.

---


> **Disclosure:** On July 16, 2026 — the day this article was published — Eli Lilly announced the acquisition of AtaiBeckley for $2.8 billion upfront. The author is an early investor in Beckley Psytech (acquired by atai Life Sciences in November 2025 to form AtaiBeckley) and holds shares that increased in value as a direct result of this transaction. The author also holds investments in the following psychedelic medicine companies mentioned in this article: MycoMedica Life Sciences, Wake Network, Radicle Science, and Tripp. These financial interests are declared in the interest of full transparency and do not alter the analysis, conclusions, or calls to action in this letter.

> **EDITOR'S SUMMARY:** On July 14, 2026 — the same day Eli Lilly announced a $2.8 billion upfront acquisition of psychedelic biotech AtaiBeckley — Dr. Samuel Lee was charged with **second-degree-felony manslaughter** for the February 2025 death of Tina Sodhi during a self-branded "Heart Protocol" ceremony in Miami Beach. The author is an early investor in Beckley Psytech, the company that merged with atai Life Sciences to form AtaiBeckley, and a 20-year acquaintance of Rick Doblin. This open letter calls for five minimum safety standards and a citizen medicine movement.

Tina Sodhi was 51 years old. She paid $2,000 to attend a three-day retreat at Sabia Wellness House in Miami Beach. She signed a waiver. She trusted someone with her life. She was found unresponsive in a rooftop sauna in February 2025. She was pronounced dead at the scene.

The Miami-Dade Medical Examiner (ruling: July 2025) determined she died from ~~extreme dehydration~~ **hyponatremic dehydration** caused by a simultaneous combination of MDMA, ketamine, and DMT — plus a ZenCleanz parasite cleanse administered before the ceremony at Lee's instruction — in prolonged sauna confinement. Dr. Samuel Lee, the licensed psychiatrist who administered those compounds, has been charged with second-degree felony manslaughter. Court records also show Lee told an officer he was not performing the ceremony under his medical license — and his Florida medical license was expired at the time of Tina Sodhi's death.

I am deeply sad writing this. That is where I need to start.

Ask yourself: if you had been in that room, what would you have done differently? And more importantly — what would have stopped you from walking in?

---

## Rick — This Moment Belongs to You

You founded [MAPS](https://maps.org) in 1986 because the DEA placed MDMA in Schedule I, overriding its own administrative law judge's recommendation that it remain available for therapeutic use. You spent four decades building the scientific, legal, and cultural foundations for the responsible use of these medicines.

This month, you said something that stopped me:

> *"We are closer than ever to psychedelics becoming legal medicines again, but what's emerging looks different from what I spent 40 years fighting for. My biggest concern now is no longer whether these therapies will be approved, but what they will look like when they arrive, and who will be able to access them. Companies are increasingly minimizing or eliminating the therapeutic component entirely, treating the drug as the product and everything around it as a cost to be cut."*
>
> — **Rick Doblin, Ph.D.**, MAPS 40th Anniversary Statement, April 2026

That warning — "treating the drug as the product and everything around it as a cost to be cut" — is the precise mechanism that killed Tina Sodhi. Dr. Lee did not eliminate the therapeutic component. He replaced it with a brand. He called it the "Heart Protocol." He charged $2,000 for access. He invented, packaged, and sold an untested compound stack as a breakthrough experience. Lee's Eternal Life Tribe had over 4,000 paying members at $55/month — a recurring revenue model built entirely on ceremonial authority.

That inversion — product over practice, novelty over wisdom, brand over reverence — is what this letter is about.

---


## Today Is July 14, 2026

This morning, [Eli Lilly announced a $2.8 billion acquisition of AtaiBeckley](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/16/eli-lilly-to-buy-psychedelics-maker-ataibeckley-2point8-billion.html) — the psychedelic biotech formed when atai Life Sciences acquired Beckley Psytech in November 2025 — a company I was a proud early investor in. It is the largest single psychedelic medicine transaction in history. Big pharma has arrived.

On this same day, Dr. Samuel Lee faces a ~~manslaughter charge~~ **second-degree-felony manslaughter** charge for Tina Sodhi's death. His jury trial is scheduled for **October 2026**. Maximum sentence: **15 years**.

Dr. Lee is not a fringe figure. He earned his MD at Loma Linda University School of Medicine. He completed his psychiatry residency at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center and the University of Washington. He was board-certified by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology since 2013. He worked as a psychiatrist at Kaiser Permanente. He was medical director at a licensed treatment center in Sedona, Arizona. He has a podcast. He has a following. He has a curriculum vitae that most practitioners in this field would envy.

None of that is a defense. It is an indictment.

[Read the full case file — Dr. Lee's license history, legal exposure, and the Heart Protocol business model →](/blog/the-case-file-dr-samuel-lee)

## The Body Does Not Care About Your Brand

I have invested in [MAPS](https://maps.org), [MycoMedica Life Sciences](https://mycomedica.com) (co-founded with Paul Stamets), [AtaiBeckley](https://ataibeckley.com), [Wake Network](https://wakenetwork.com), [Radicle Science](https://radicle.science), [TRIPP](https://tripp.com), and others. I have sat with these medicines myself. I am not an expert. I am a student. That distinction matters enormously here.

I recently began building the [Psychedelic Readiness Index](https://tonygreenberg.com/psychedelic-readiness-index) — a clinical screening tool covering 26 medicines across 6 safety domains — because pharmacological sequencing, interaction risk, and the balance between synthetic and natural substances is dangerously under-addressed in the retreat and ceremony space.

## Matthew Perry Died the Same Way

[Matthew Perry died in October 2023](https://www.cnbc.com/2023/12/15/matthew-perry-cause-of-death-revealed.html). Found face down in his hot tub. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner determined the cause of death was the acute effects of ketamine. His blood concentration — 3,271 nanograms per milliliter — was within the range used for surgical general anesthesia. He was alone. He was in hot water. He was dissociated from his own body. He drowned.

# Tina Sodhi Died in a Sauna.
# She Didn't Have To.

On February 10, 2025, Tina Sodhi paid $2,000 to attend a three-day "Heart Protocol" ceremony at a wellness home in Miami Beach. She was administered MDMA and ketamine. She was found unresponsive in a rooftop sauna.

The Miami-Dade Medical Examiner ruled her death: ~~dehydration~~ **hyponatremic dehydration** from the combination of MDMA, ketamine, DMT, prolonged sauna confinement, and a pre-ceremony ZenCleanz cleanse administered at Lee's instruction. She had signed a waiver. It didn't save her. It didn't save the doctor either — Dr. Samuel Lee was charged with felony manslaughter on July 14, 2026.

She was not the first. She will not be the last — unless this industry decides to govern itself before the government does it for us.

What follows are not guidelines. They are the minimum standard of care this field must adopt publicly, immediately, and without exception.

---

## The Six Laws of Conscious Medicine

*These are not guidelines. They are the minimum standard of care this field must adopt publicly, immediately, and without exception.*

---

**LAW I — Water and heat kill when combined with dissociative compounds. No exceptions.** Tina Sodhi died because MDMA and ketamine were administered before sauna exposure. MDMA elevates core body temperature and suppresses heat regulation. A sauna is not spiritual in this context. It is fatal. No ceremony overrides this. No waiver makes it legal. No brand name makes it safe.

**LAW II — Compound stacking without peer-reviewed safety data is experimentation. Name it that.** MDMA, ketamine, and DMT did not kill Tina Sodhi separately. They killed her together — in a combination that had never been studied, presented as a "Heart Protocol." If there is no published safety data on the specific combination at the specific doses you are administering, you are running an experiment. Your participants did not sign up for an experiment.

**LAW III — A waiver is not informed consent.** Tina Sodhi signed a waiver. She did not understand that MDMA plus ketamine plus a sauna could kill her — because no one told her. Real informed consent requires a sober explanation of every compound and its interaction risks, written contraindications, and the right to withdraw at any stage without social pressure or financial penalty. A signature is not the same thing. Her family knows what the difference is.

**LAW IV — Credentials do not replace lineage, training, and humility.** The most dangerous practitioner in this space right now is the one who completed a weekend certification last year and charges $3,000 a seat. Ask your facilitator: Who trained you? How long? Are you still in supervision? If they cannot answer all three without defensiveness, you have your answer.

**LAW V — These medicines are singular teachers. You do not stack teachers and expect coherence.** Every tradition that has worked with these plants for centuries holds one inviolable principle: one medicine, one container, one teacher at a time. The moment you combine two medicines in one ceremony, you have stepped outside every map that exists. You are no longer facilitating. You are improvising with someone else's nervous system.

**LAW VI — A practice improves. A product just sells.** The day you stop asking "what did I miss?" is the day you become dangerous. Tina Sodhi's death was not an accident. It was the result of a practitioner who had answers instead of questions. If you are more focused on your next cohort than your last client's integration — you are running a business, not a practice. One of them has a body count.

---

**If you run retreats:** Post these six laws publicly. On your website. Before the booking page. If you will not stand behind them publicly, examine why.

**If you refer clients:** You are accountable for where you send them. Ask every operator you refer to whether they will sign these laws. Publish who will and who will not.

**If you are a client:** You have the right to ask every one of these questions before you enter any container. A facilitator who cannot answer them clearly and without defensiveness is not ready to hold you. Walk away. Tina Sodhi paid $2,000. She paid with her life.

---

> The industry will not self-regulate through good intentions. It will self-regulate through standards that the best practitioners hold publicly — and the worst are publicly measured against. Tina Sodhi deserved these laws before February 10, 2025. The next person deserves them today.

*— TonyG*

---

*Share this. Ask every facilitator you work with to sign it publicly. If they won't — that is your answer. And now you know.*

---

> **Featured Response — July 16, 2026**
> 
> *"Off-label prescribing is when a doctor prescribes an FDA-approved medicine to treat a condition, or in a way, that the FDA has not officially approved. It depends upon and trusts the physicians', the professionals', judgement.*
> 
> *Professional judgement is all too commonly diminished by good intentions, when the prescriber does not say 'no' to a patient in sometimes desperate need. Or whose pockets are full of cash and clout, as is suggested in the tragedy of patient Tina Sodhi and physician Dr. Samuel Lee.*
> 
> *'Let the buyer beware' places responsibility and risk upon the end user, in this case, the patient. Better, I suggest, is trust, but verify — which suggests, do not trust blindly because of a degree upon the wall.*
> 
> *Hallucinogenics are now soaked in hype and money and a desire for magic. While studies show value for PTSD and depression resistant to treatment, any one practitioner with their own special treatment should be examined — both by the patient and the professional associations — and given an opportunity to support their protocol before being let loose upon the public."*
> 
> — **Dr. Stephen Scappa**, 50+ years guiding peak-performance humans, July 16, 2026


## What These Medicines Actually Teach

As I wrote in [DoubleBlind](https://doubleblindmag.com/psychedelics-could-become-extractive-capitalism/) in 2021, the ancient Peruvian concept of ayni — sacred reciprocity — teaches that if we take without giving, we hurt ourselves and can become sick. Lee took $2,000 from a woman who trusted him with her life. He took the spiritual legitimacy of traditions that took centuries to develop. He gave nothing back except a pharmacological environment that guaranteed harm.

He approached as the teacher. He made himself the medicine. He branded his invention and charged for access. That inversion is what killed Tina Sodhi.

---


## The Paradox of This Watershed Day

[Eli Lilly's $2.8 billion acquisition of AtaiBeckley](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-16/lilly-to-buy-psychedelic-firm-ataibeckley-for-up-to-3-8-billion) validates what this field can become at its best. BPL-003 — a nasally administered 5-MeO-DMT treatment for treatment-resistant depression — is administered in a clinic, under monitoring, for about two hours. Single compound. Safe environment. Supervised. That is what responsible looks like.

And on this same day, Tina Sodhi has been dead for more than a year.

Rick, you also said this month: *"After four decades, I remain genuinely optimistic that psychedelic-assisted therapies will once again become legal. But legality was never the point. Healing was."*

That sentence is the entire argument of this letter. Legality was never the point. Healing was. And healing requires the humility to keep practicing.

---


## A Deep Bow: Ron Beller

Before the disclaimer, a recognition that belongs here.

**[Ron Beller](https://www.aspenpublicradio.org/ideas-speakers-lectures/2024-06-03/aps2024-fireside-chat-rick-doblin-ph-d-with-ron-beller)** — Goldman Sachs partner turned executive coach, founding member of the Psychedelic Science Funders Collaborative, board member of MAPS Israel, and Rick Doblin's personal coach (watch their [fireside chat at the Wheeler](https://www.aspenpublicradio.org/ideas-speakers-lectures/2024-06-03/aps2024-fireside-chat-rick-doblin-ph-d-with-ron-beller)) — has been one of the quiet architects of the psychedelic medicine movement's credibility. Not from a stage. Not from a press release. From the inside, over years, doing the unglamorous work of holding space for the people who hold space for everyone else.

## A Note on My Standing to Write This

**Disclosure and accountability:** For over 20 years, Tony Greenberg has been a personal acquaintance of Rick Doblin and has had direct visibility inside MAPS — as an observer, supporter, and investor in MAPS Public Benefit Corporation (MAPS PBC). He is also an investor in MAPS Public Benefit Corporation (MAPS PBC), MycoMedica Life Sciences, AtaiBeckley, Wake Network, Radicle Science, and TRIPP.

This piece was written with AI assistance to raise the baton faster. Conscious satisficing — moving at the speed of relevance rather than waiting for perfection — is a principle explored in depth in [Human Operating System](/blog/human-operating-system). This essay embodies that principle: speed over polish, accountability over silence.

---

# Five Cups: Who Profits When the Government Tells You to Drink More?

### The American Heart Association just gave America a second coffee. The industry is celebrating. Your bones are not. And somewhere in Silicon Valley, a VC is already building a Five-Cup Subscription Box.

---

Every generation has that family member who texts you at 8am with a hot investment tip. The tip is always something the news said was good for you. Coffee. Red wine. Eggs. Bitcoin. Whatever just got a government green light that morning. The logic is airtight: government says it's healthy, people will buy more, buy the machine, buy the stock, get in early.

They are not wrong that there is money in it. They are just asking the wrong question. And so is the government.

This morning the American Heart Association published a landmark statement in the journal *Circulation*. The headline: **up to five cups of coffee per day is safe for most adults**, potentially linked to lower risk of heart failure, stroke, and type 2 diabetes. America grabbed its fourth cup and exhaled. The National Coffee Association's CEO declared that coffee drinkers "live longer, healthier, happier lives." The stock tickers twitched. The Keurig pods flew off shelves.

Let's talk about what they buried in paragraph nine.

## What the Fine Print Actually Says

The real sweet spot the AHA identified is **two to four cups** — not five. Five appears "safe," which is a clinical way of saying it probably won't kill you on a Tuesday. Benefits plateau or reverse beyond four cups, and side effects — disrupted sleep, elevated anxiety, blood pressure spikes — become more likely.

More critically: **these heart-healthy findings apply strictly to paper-filtered or instant coffee.** Not espresso. Not French press. Not Turkish. Those methods retain a compound called cafestol that actively raises LDL cholesterol — the kind that quietly clogs arteries while you congratulate yourself for drinking "heart-healthy" coffee.

> So the government said five cups is fine, as long as it's filtered, without sugar, without cream, without syrups, and you have no existing heart condition, no genetic caffeine sensitivity, are not pregnant, are not a teenager, and are not taking certain medications. **Other than that: drink up, America.**

The report also, quietly, says nothing about what coffee does to the rest of your body — specifically your skeleton.

## Your Heart Might Survive It. Your Bones Are a Different Story.

For every 150mg of caffeine consumed, research shows the body may lose approximately 4–5mg of calcium through increased urinary excretion and reduced intestinal absorption. That loss compounds daily over months and years. Studies have found that postmenopausal women who consume more than 300mg of caffeine daily — about three cups — show significantly lower bone mineral density in their spine and hip regions.

Human studies suggest caffeine may also interfere with the activity of vitamin D receptors and bone-forming enzymes in osteoblasts. Less vitamin D receptor activity means less calcium absorbed from everything you eat. The AHA was measuring hearts. Nobody measured bones. The AHA study says nothing about the slow-motion calcium drain happening one cup at a time.

> "Safe" is not the same as optimal. A permission slip issued to an industry, laundered through science, and delivered to consumers as health news — is still a permission slip.

## Who Actually Wins When the Ceiling Goes Up

Let's follow the money. **66% of Americans had a coffee in the past day** — that's roughly 220 million cups. The US coffee market is worth over $100 billion annually. When the government raises the daily ceiling from four to five cups, that is not a health recommendation. That is a market expansion event.

The food and beverage industry has given close to $200 million to Political Action Committees and Congressional members over recent three-year cycles. Industry funds studies, cultivates nutritionists, and shapes the language that becomes policy. The AHA's own funding streams include industry partnerships. This is not conspiracy — it is the ordinary mechanics of how guidelines get made in America.

When five cups gets the green light, [Starbucks](https://www.starbucks.com) sells more Venti drip. Nestlé moves more pods. Keurig machines fly. The farmer in Ethiopia who grew the bean still earns under $2 a day. GDP goes up. Bone density, calcium absorption, and meaningful farmer equity go sideways. The machine is a great buy for the company that makes it. Less so for the body that runs on it.

## What You Should Actually Drink in the Morning

If the goal is a morning ritual that genuinely upgrades your cognition, protects your body, supports mineral absorption, and doesn't require a five-paragraph government disclaimer — here are the alternatives that actually hold up.

**[Ceremonial Matcha](https://teaperfectionist.com/best-matcha-tea/)** — L-theanine plus ~70mg caffeine creates sustained alertness without the jitter spike. 137x more antioxidants than brewed green tea. Protects rather than depletes calcium. The Japanese have been right about this for 800 years. Get authentic Uji origin — anything from China at under $10 is powdered nostalgia. (~$1.50/serving. Value: Exceptional.)

**[Lion's Mane + Cordyceps](https://us.dirteaworld.com)** — Lion's Mane stimulates nerve growth factor — actual brain tissue repair, not marketing copy. Cordyceps boosts mitochondrial oxygen efficiency. Together they deliver focused energy that compounds long-term rather than burning adrenal credit you'll pay back by 3pm. (~$40–65/month. Value: Strong.)

**[Cacao + Reishi](https://mudwtr.com)** — Raw cacao carries theobromine — a gentler, longer-lasting stimulant than caffeine with zero calcium disruption. Reishi is the stress modulator: it doesn't rev you up, it stabilizes the baseline so you can actually think. This is what a morning ritual feels like when it's designed for humans, not productivity theater. (~$30–50/month. Value: Good.)

**[Yerba Mate](https://www.guayaki.com)** — ~80mg caffeine, plus theobromine and theophylline — a more balanced stimulant triplex than coffee alone. That is the only place on earth where that introduction is even possible ✦ a Kenyan woman behind a coffee counter in Aspen, and the man who has spent his career investing in the country she came from, both within walking distance of each other on a Tuesday.

That is a GemSpark. That is exactly what it is.

Coffee is the only thing on earth that can do this. Not LinkedIn. Not Davos. Not a conference room with a view. A cup. A counter. Two people on opposite ends of a supply chain, briefly occupying the same moment as equals.

The distance between the person who grows it and the person who drinks it is where most of the value gets extracted and most of the meaning gets lost. BrewSoul (https://brewsoul.com) is trying to close that gap.

⁂

Further Reading

These are the threads worth pulling after this one:

The Psychedelics Could Become Extractive Capitalism (/blog/psychedelics-could-become-extractive-capitalism) · Written for DoubleBlind in 2021. The same pattern: an industry captures a wellness movement, launders it through science, and sells volume. The warning was already there.

ImpactSoul (https://impactsoul.is) · The thesis behind this essay made investable. Regenerative vs. extractive. Transparent vs. opaque.

BrewSoul Coffee Intelligence (https://tonygreenberg.com/brewsoul) · 107 specialty coffees scored on cupping quality, mold testing, farmer transparency, and actual value. The antidote to government-endorsed volume guidance.

Outlive by Peter Attia (https://www.amazon.com/Outlive-Longevity-Peter-Attia-MD/dp/0593236599) · The science of longevity without the biohacking vanity. Chapter on caffeine metabolism and CYP1A2 genetics is essential reading.

Count Down by Shanna Swan (https://www.amazon.com/Count-Down-Threatening-Reproductive-Development/dp/1982113669) · The definitive book on how chemicals are reshaping human biology. Same pattern, different compound.

The Omnivore's Dilemma by Michael Pollan (https://www.amazon.com/Omnivores-Dilemma-Natural-History-Meals/dp/0143038583) · The original follow-the-money investigation into how industrial food systems captured government nutrition guidance.

Five Questions Worth Sitting With

These are not rhetorical. Leave your answer in the comments ✦ the most interesting responses will be featured in the next BrewSoul dispatch.

Most morning routines were assembled from marketing, not intention. Trace yours back. Who told you five cups was the goal? What were they selling?

2. If your CYP1A2 gene variant meant you metabolized caffeine slowly, would you change anything?
Slow metabolizers face significantly elevated cardiovascular risk from high caffeine intake. The test costs $99. Most people have never taken it. Why not?

3. What is the last thing you consumed where you knew exactly who grew it, what they were paid, and how it was processed?
Not the brand story. The actual supply chain. If you can't name one thing, what does that tell you about the system you're participating in?

4. At what point does "safe" become a good enough standard for what you put in your body every single morning?
Safe is a floor, not a ceiling. What would optimal look like, and what would it cost you to find out?

5. If the government raised the daily recommended limit on something you currently avoid, would you reconsider it?
This is the real question. Because that's exactly what happened with coffee ✦ and most people updated their behavior without asking who updated the guideline.
